[=Known Limits and Extension Points=]

This file documents no theoretical risks, only limits that are directly visible in the current code or in verified tests.

The prioritized implementation order for those limits is documented in [<43_next_work.wiki>].

[=Verified Limits=]

[| [*Area*] | [*State in code*] | [*Practical impact*] |]
[| Conditional types | [.txt|mVM_Type.Cond(...).], [.txt|IsCond(...).], and [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.] for [.txt|TypeCond.] are unfinished | [.txt|TypeCond.] exists syntactically, but not as a robust end-to-end feature |]
[| Runtime type values | [.txt|mVM_Data.tOpCode.], [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.], and [.txt|mVM.Step(...).] are not aligned: the VM executes only [.txt|TypeFree.], [.txt|TypePair.], [.txt|TypeSet.], [.txt|TypeRecursive.], and [.txt|TypeGeneric.], while the generator already handles more cases and still throws on [.txt|TypeCond.] | type expressions as runtime values are only partially reliable |]
[| Runtime match opcodes | [.txt|mIL_AST.], [.txt|mIL_Parser.], and [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.] all expose [.txt|TryAsType.] and [.txt|TryAsRef.], but [.txt|mVM.Step(...).] has no execution case for either one, and [.txt|mVM_Data.tDataType.] has no [.txt|Ref.] value kind | IL/runtime matching support is broader on paper than it is in the executing VM |]
[| Generic type application across modules | [.txt|mModule_Tests.Maybe.] fails at [.txt|.tMaybe tIn.] while [.txt|mModule.Init(...).] is still compiling [.txt|Modules/Maybe.SPO.] through [.txt|mSPO_Parser.Module.ParseText(...).ToILT().] and [.txt|mSPO_AST_Types.AsVM_Type(GenericApplyType).] | successful generic support in regressions does not yet mean stable module libraries, and this specific failure is earlier than IL execution or VM runtime |]
[| Regression test discovery | [.txt|mRegression_Tests.] resolves [.txt|Regression.Tests.] through [.txt|mFS.CWD().] and prints [.txt|Folder not found: mFS+tFolder.] on a miss | running [.txt|mRunTests.] from the repo root silently drops the regression suite unless the current working directory is changed to [.txt|SPO_CS/.] first |]
[| Subtyping | [.txt|mVM_Type.IsSubType(...).] still throws [.txt|NotImplementedException.] for [.txt|Any.], [.txt|Var.], [.txt|Ref.], and [.txt|Cond.] | parts of the type system are parseable more broadly than they are actually decidable |]
[| Recursive proc materialization | [.txt|mVM.Step(...).] currently uses [.txt|Count = 1.] for [.txt|DefRecProcs.] | mutual recursion between multiple values remains a risk area |]
[| Prefix/field keys | prefixes and record fields are mapped to [.txt|tNat32.] via [.txt|PrefixHash().] | theoretical hash collisions are not yet ruled out |]
[| Type desugaring | [.txt|mSPO_Desugar.DesugarType(...).] actively normalizes only tuple types | some type forms survive in their surface shape deep into the backend |]

[=What the Tests Already Cover Cleanly=]

- parser and printer for IL commands and IL type commands
- SPO end-to-end for literals, records, match, recursion, and [.txt|§VAR.]
- recursive and generic type syntax in regressions
- library modules [.txt|Std.], [.txt|Char.], and [.txt|Text.]

[=What Is Documented Cautiously on Purpose=]

The following language and architecture forms are visible in the code, but
should not be understood as broadly secured "finished features":

- [.txt|§INTERFACE.] type syntax
- runtime evaluation of all type literals
- runtime execution of every emitted match opcode
- multi-proc recursive groups as runtime values
- generic library modules with type application across module boundaries

[=Highest-Value Clarification=]

The current [.txt|Maybe.] failure is important because it narrows the problem more
than the short error message suggests:

- verified fact: [.txt|07_12_GenericTypes.] passes all three regression checks
- verified fact: [.txt|mModule_Tests.Maybe.] fails in [.txt|Modules/Maybe.SPO.] at [.txt|.tMaybe tIn.]
- verified fact: that failure is raised during the [.txt|.SPO -> .ILT.] validation path before the module reaches [.txt|mVM.Run(...).]

Inference from the source and error text, to verify during implementation:

- because the failing code path is [.txt|mSPO_AST_Types.AsVM_Type(GenericApplyType).] and the message prints [.txt|_tMaybe....], the immediate issue is likely in how named generic type constructors are resolved or materialized during module compilation, not in opcode execution

[=Concrete Extension Path=]

[.mermaid
|flowchart TD
|	FEATURE["New language or runtime feature"] --> PARSE["Tokenizer / Parser"]
|	FEATURE --> TYPE["mVM_Type + mSPO_AST_Types"]
|	FEATURE --> DES["mSPO_Desugar"]
|	FEATURE --> IL["mSPO2IL + mIL_AST"]
|	FEATURE --> OPC["mIL_GenerateOpcodes"]
|	FEATURE --> VM["mVM / mVM_Data"]
|	FEATURE --> TEST["Tests + Regressions + Modules"]
.]

In this repository, a feature only truly exists once all affected layers have been carried through:

o 1. Syntax
o 2. Type analysis
o 3. Lowering
o 4. Opcode generation
o 5. VM execution
o 6. Regression or module tests

For type-related features there is an additional practical rule: verify the opcode enum, the IL generator, and [.txt|mVM.Step(...).] together. In the current codebase those three layers do not automatically move in lockstep.

[=Recommended Order for Extensions=]

[=1. Stabilize Generic Modules=]

The reproducible [.txt|Maybe.] gap is the best concrete place to harden generics across library boundaries.

[=2. Complete the Type System=]

If [.txt|Any.], [.txt|Var.], [.txt|Ref.], or [.txt|Cond.] should be presented as frontend features, then [.txt|mVM_Type.IsSubType(...).] needs a robust implementation first.

[=3. Close the Runtime Type-Value Gap=]

If type literals are supposed to be exportable or manipulable as runtime data, the missing [.txt|Type*.] cases in [.txt|mVM.Step(...).] need to be completed.

[=4. Harden Recursion and Prefix Identity=]

Multi-recursion and hash-based prefixes are currently the two clearest runtime risk areas below the language surface.

[=5. Make Verification Less CWD-Sensitive=]

The regression harness should resolve its fixture folder from a stable project anchor instead of [.txt|mFS.CWD().], and its missing-folder warning should print the resolved path rather than the type name [.txt|mFS+tFolder.].

[=Good Extension Points in Code=]

- [.txt|mSPO_Parser.]
  when new surface syntax is added
- [.txt|mSPO_Desugar.]
  when sugar should be reduced to existing core forms
- [.txt|mSPO_AST_Types.]
  when new scope or type rules are needed
- [.txt|mSPO2IL.]
  when a feature exists in the AST but does not yet reach IL
- [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.]
  when IL already exists but still has no VM operation
- [.txt|mVM.]
  when runtime behavior or new type opcodes are missing
- [.txt|mRegression_Tests.] and [.txt|mModule_Tests.]
  when a feature should be secured with real artifacts
